item.title: Arts Council of Northern Ireland: Artists' International Development Fund for Organisations (2026)
item.description:
Organisation: Arts Council of Northern Ireland

Location: Applicant organisations must be based in Northern Ireland; the funded activity takes place internationally, with an overseas partner or host.

Award: GBP 1,000 to 7,000. Covers art materials, residency costs, travel (mileage at 25.7p per mile plus airfare), artistic and technical fees for production or post-production, venue hire, project equipment capped at 50 percent of the request value, and IT equipment up to GBP 1,200 for laptops or GBP 500 for tablets. No application fee.

Duration: Short, early-stage international development activity.

Deadline: 30 Jul 2026

The Artists' International Development Fund (Organisations) is Arts Council of Northern Ireland's route for NI-based arts organisations to take a first substantive step into international working. It is the organisations counterpart to the individual-artist AIDF under the Support for the Individual Artist Programme, which is a separate scheme with its own amount band. Grants run GBP 1,000 to 7,000 and cover art materials, residency costs, travel including airfare and mileage, artistic and technical fees for production or post-production, venue hire, and equipment capped at 50 percent of the request value. The deadline is Thursday 30 July 2026 at 12:00 noon, and the online system closes precisely at noon. Applicants must be NI-based, must have received recognition for their work there, and must not already have extensive international experience. The application must evidence genuine interest from an overseas partner or host, so a confirmed international invitation, residency offer or presentation opportunity is effectively a precondition.

item.title: BFI National Lottery Impact Feature Funding (Higher-Budget Features)
item.description:
Organisation: British Film Institute (BFI Filmmaking Fund, National Lottery)

Location: United Kingdom (applications must come from a limited company registered and centrally managed in the UK)

Award: Up to GBP 1,250,000, the largest single award in the current BFI portfolio, though the BFI notes it does not expect to support many projects at the maximum level. Production budgets from GBP 1M to GBP 15M for experienced directors, GBP 3.5M to GBP 15M for debut directors. No application fee.

Duration: Single production award; apply at least 20 weeks before the first day of principal photography.

Deadline: Rolling / undated

Impact is the higher-budget production strand of the BFI Filmmaking Fund and carries the largest award available in the current BFI portfolio at up to GBP 1.25 million. It sits above the Discovery strand in scale, serving experienced directors with production budgets from GBP 1 million to GBP 15 million, and debut directors whose budgets exceed GBP 3.5 million. UNLIKE DISCOVERY, Impact accepts applications on a continuous rolling basis with no round structure and no published closing date, though applicants must submit at least 20 weeks before principal photography begins. SELECTION is explicitly criteria-driven: projects must address at least three of the BFI's stated aims, covering equity and inclusion, audience or cultural impact, talent development, creative risk, production activity across the UK nations and regions, and environmental sustainability. ELIGIBILITY: applications must come from a limited company registered and centrally managed in the UK, so individuals cannot apply. A dedicated producer is always required, though unlike Discovery the writer and director may be the same person. Directing credits must be evidenced. No explicit nationality or residency test for the director or writer is published. NOTE: the BFI cautions that maximum-level awards are rare, so realistic requests will typically fall well below the GBP 1.25 million ceiling.

Open call details

item.title: BFI National Lottery Development Funding (Feature Script and Package Development)
item.description:
Organisation: British Film Institute (BFI Filmmaking Fund, National Lottery)

Location: United Kingdom (producers must apply through a limited company registered at Companies House)

Award: Award amounts are not published on the fund page. No application fee.

Duration: Development period varies by project. Open year-round with an annual closure from 1 to 30 April, plus occasional short closures during busy or holiday periods.

Deadline: Rolling / undated

Development Funding is the earliest-stage strand of the BFI Filmmaking Fund, supporting original live action and animated feature films through script and package development to the point where they are viable candidates for production finance. It is aimed at distinctive fiction projects from what the BFI calls 'adventurous storytellers', across a wide range of genres rather than a single house style. UNLIKE DISCOVERY, it does not operate in rounds: applications are accepted year-round, with the only fixed interruption being an annual closure through the month of April, plus occasional short pauses during periods of high demand or holidays. ELIGIBILITY: the application must be made by a producer through a limited company registered at Companies House, so unincorporated individuals are ineligible. Nationality and residency requirements are not published on the fund page. NOTE: award amounts are not published, so the ceiling should be treated as unknown rather than assumed. Successful applicants are required to publicly acknowledge National Lottery support in project credits and materials.

Open call details

item.title: Arts Council of Wales: Festivals (2026 rounds)
item.description:
Organisation: Arts Council of Wales

Location: Festival must take place in Wales and demonstrate cultural value to the local community. Welsh language integration expected.

Award: GBP 500 to 100,000 across four tiers: Small up to GBP 10,000; Large up to GBP 35,000 (1+ year track record); Large up to GBP 60,000 (3+ years, regional significance, 2+ day programme); Large up to GBP 100,000 (5+ years, national significance). Co-financing mandatory: the Council funds a maximum of 75 percent of eligible costs, so at least 25 percent of project income must come from non-Arts Council and non-Lottery sources, of which no more than 10 percent may be in-kind. No application fee.

Duration: One or two years of festival activity; two-year applications require a track record and development plan.

Deadline: Closed 29 Jul 2026

Festivals is one of the new National Lottery programmes Arts Council of Wales launched on 13 April 2026, and it is the clearest organisation-facing route for funding a public festival in Wales. It supports focused, time-limited festivals delivering high-quality arts programmes to broad audiences, in a single artform or mixed artforms, with preference given to festivals that commission, create and present new artistic work. Grants run GBP 500 to 100,000 across four tiers, with the tier ceiling tied to how long the festival has been established. Match funding is mandatory: the Council covers at most 75 percent of eligible costs and in-kind support is capped at 10 percent. There are two deadlines in 2026, both at 1pm: Wednesday 29 July 2026 and Wednesday 16 December 2026. TIMING RULE: a minimum of twelve working weeks must fall between the deadline and the project start date, so activity applied for in the July round cannot begin before roughly late October 2026. Retrospective costs are ineligible. Individual artists cannot apply.

Open call details

item.title: Arts Council of Wales: Create and Engage (2026 rounds)
item.description:
Organisation: Arts Council of Wales

Location: Projects must take place mainly in Wales. Individual applicants must be Wales-based; organisations outside the UK may take part as partners provided a UK-based eligible organisation leads.

Award: Small awards up to GBP 10,000; Large awards GBP 10,001 to 60,000; exceptionally up to GBP 100,000 with prior approval from an Arts Council manager. At least 10 percent of project costs must come from non-Arts Council and non-Lottery sources. No application fee.

Duration: Project-length; activity must not already be underway at the point of application.

Deadline: Closed 29 Jul 2026

Create and Engage is Arts Council of Wales's general-purpose National Lottery programme for making and presenting arts work, launched alongside Festivals in April 2026, and is the natural fit for exhibitions, public programmes, touring and participatory events that are not structured as a festival. It funds creation, presentation, programming, touring, community participation and, for organisations only, professional development. Small awards go up to GBP 10,000 and large awards run GBP 10,001 to 60,000, with up to GBP 100,000 possible in exceptional cases with advance manager approval. At least 10 percent of project costs must come from non-Council, non-Lottery sources, a notably lighter co-financing burden than the Festivals fund's 25 percent. TIMING RULES: Small Create and Engage is rolling with no set deadlines but requires a minimum of 10 working weeks between submission and project start; Large Create and Engage has fixed 1pm deadlines on 29 July 2026, 30 September 2026 and 16 December 2026, with a minimum of 12 working weeks between deadline and project start. Non-UK organisations can participate as partners but cannot lead. Applicants cannot have an application in to more than one Arts Council fund at the same time.

Open call details

item.title: BFI National Lottery Creative Challenge Fund (Round Two)
item.description:
Organisation: British Film Institute (BFI National Lottery)

Location: United Kingdom (UK-based organisations running development programmes for UK creatives)

Award: Award amounts are not published on the fund page. No application fee.

Duration: Funded programme activity must start between 1 January and 30 June 2027 and, in most cases, be delivered within 12 months unless the applicant is running multiple editions.

Deadline: 21 Sep 2026

The Creative Challenge Fund does not fund films directly. It funds the organisations that run project-development programmes for UK creatives working on narrative, documentary or animation features, or on narrative immersive media projects. The BFI's stated aim is to decentralise development away from a small number of London-centric gatekeepers and build a wider, more resilient ecosystem of talent-development providers across the UK, with a recently added emphasis on independent producers. ELIGIBILITY: only legally constituted UK-based organisations may apply. Individual filmmakers seeking development money should look to the BFI Filmmaking Fund's Development strand instead. TIMING: Round One closed in March 2026 and has made its first awards. Round Two closes Monday 21 September 2026, with funded programme activity required to begin between 1 January and 30 June 2027. NOTE: award amounts are not published on the fund page. Successful applicants must prominently credit BFI National Lottery support.

Open call details

item.title: BFI National Lottery Discovery Feature Funding (Debut Fiction Features)
item.description:
Organisation: British Film Institute (BFI Filmmaking Fund, National Lottery)

Location: United Kingdom (applications must come from a limited company registered and centrally managed in the UK)

Award: Up to GBP 1,000,000 of National Lottery funding towards a fiction feature with a production budget between GBP 1,000,000 and GBP 3,500,000. No application fee.

Duration: Single production award; apply at least 20 weeks before the first day of principal photography. Decisions in principle within roughly 12 weeks of the round closing.

Deadline: 13 Aug 2026

Discovery is the debut-director production strand of the BFI Filmmaking Fund, awarding up to GBP 1 million towards fiction features budgeted between GBP 1 million and GBP 3.5 million. It backs first-time feature directors working alongside experienced producers, and is structured so creative risk sits with a team rather than a lone filmmaker. ELIGIBILITY: applications must be made through a limited company registered and centrally managed in the UK, so unincorporated individuals cannot apply. A dedicated lead producer with an established track record must submit, and that producer must be someone other than the writer or director. The director must be making their first fiction feature, meaning no prior feature at or above a GBP 1 million budget and no prior commercial UK or Ireland theatrical distribution of a fiction feature. At least two people must be credited across the writer, producer and director roles, all aged 18 or over and not in full-time education. Projects need a fully developed script and a runtime of at least 70 minutes. LIMITS: one application per production company, producer and director per round, and applications must arrive at least 20 weeks before the proposed first day of principal photography. ROUNDS: Round 2 closes at 5pm on Thursday 13 August 2026. Round 3 opens Thursday 12 November 2026 and closes Wednesday 16 December 2026. Successful applicants must publicly credit BFI National Lottery support.

Open call details

item.title: UK Global Screen Fund: International Distribution, Video Game Release Funding
item.description:
Organisation: British Film Institute (UK Global Screen Fund, backed by DCMS)

Location: United Kingdom (applications from the UK-based lead development studio)

Award: Non-recoupable grant towards international marketing and release activity; the award range is not published on the fund page. A cap of GBP 625,000 applies across all UKGSF strands per organisation over any three-year period. No application fee.

Duration: Single release-activity award; apply no later than eight weeks before the funded activity begins.

Deadline: 14 Aug 2026

The newest strand of the UK Global Screen Fund extends the fund's international-distribution logic from film into UK independent narrative video games. It supports marketing and release activity for games with demonstrable international appeal and sales potential, awarding non-recoupable grants to help UK studios reach overseas players. ELIGIBILITY: applications must be made by the UK-based development studio deemed the lead developer for the game, and only narrative video games qualify. One application per game. The wider UKGSF requirement that applicants be independent screen-sector companies registered and centrally managed in the UK applies. TIMING: the round opened 14 May 2026 and closes at 12pm on Friday 14 August 2026, making it one of the few hard-deadline BFI opportunities currently live. Separately, applications must be filed at least eight weeks before the funded activity starts, so a game releasing in early autumn may fall outside the window even if the application lands before 14 August. NOTE: award amounts are not published on the fund page, so treat the range as unknown rather than estimated. A cumulative cap of GBP 625,000 per organisation across all UK Global Screen Fund strands over any three-year period also applies.

Open call details

item.title: LSE Research Officer: DigiPulse, Digital Futures for Children Centre
item.description:
Organisation: London School of Economics and Political Science (LSE), Department of Media and Communications

Location: London, UK (hybrid working)

Award: GBP 43,277 to 51,714 per year inclusive of London allowance, with potential to progress to GBP 55,497. Full-time (1.0 FTE), funded until December 2028. Benefits: occupational pension scheme, generous annual leave, hybrid working, training and development. No application fee.

Duration: Full-time fixed-term post, funded until December 2028

Deadline: Closed 22 Jul 2026

DigiPulse is a three-year longitudinal, international research project in LSE's Digital Futures for Children centre investigating the real-time relationships between children's smartphone use and their wellbeing, with data collected in the UK, Brazil and Kenya. The project combines passive smartphone tracking, Ecological Momentary Assessment (EMA) and longitudinal surveys with around 750 children and young people aged 10-17. THE ROLE: the Research Officer plays a central part in project management, development, data collection and analysis, with particular responsibility for developing and refining EMA instruments, contributing to the research literature and hypotheses, supporting participatory and consultative work with children, and conducting statistical analysis and producing findings, working closely with partners in the UK, Brazil and Kenya. REQUIREMENTS: a completed PhD in a relevant discipline (e.g. media and communications, psychology, psychiatry, sociology, education, or computational/data social science); experience developing surveys or questionnaire instruments; experience designing or conducting longitudinal research studies; and experience with EMA, experience-sampling or other intensive longitudinal data collection methods. APPLY via jobs.lse.ac.uk; questions to k.g.ringmar-sylwander@lse.ac.uk. Closing date 22 July 2026 (23:59 UK time); late applications are not accepted.

Open call details

item.title: Sarabande Foundation: Studio Residency 2026/27 (UK-based only)
item.description:
Organisation: Sarabande Foundation

Location: London, United Kingdom. Requires a UK address and right to work in the UK; no visa sponsorship.

Award: Heavily subsidised studio space (GBP 1 per sq ft per month including utilities), mentoring from industry experts, pro bono business support, and access to the Sarabande network. Free to apply.

Duration: Residencies start November 2026.

Deadline: 01 Aug 2026

The Sarabande Foundation, founded by Lee Alexander McQueen, offers subsidised London studio residencies for creatives across disciplines (fine art, fashion, design, digital), with structured mentoring and pro bono expert support. ELIGIBILITY: applicants must have a UK address and the right to work in the UK; the foundation cannot sponsor visas. Deadline 1 August 2026.

item.title: CRASSH 25th Anniversary Exhibition: Knowledge in a Fractured World
item.description:
Organisation: CRASSH, University of Cambridge

Location: Cambridge, United Kingdom (Alison Richard Building). Open worldwide.

Award: Exhibition from 5 October to 11 December 2026; no commission taken on sales. Free to enter.

Duration: Exhibition 5 October to 11 December 2026.

Deadline: 31 Jul 2026

The Centre for Research in the Arts, Social Sciences and Humanities (CRASSH) at the University of Cambridge marks its 25th anniversary with an open-call exhibition on the theme Knowledge in a Fractured World: how knowledge is produced, contested, and shared in a fragmented age. Accepts 2D, 3D, video, film, and sound work; a strong thematic fit for critical data and research-based practices. Open worldwide, free to enter, no commission on sales. Deadline 31 July 2026.

item.title: Corridor: DAISY CHAIN Artist Commission (Adur, West Sussex)
item.description:
Organisation: Corridor Projects

Location: Adur and Worthing, West Sussex, UK. Open to a socially-engaged artist based in the South East of England working with moving image / lens-based media.

Award: GBP 4,200 artist fee (inclusive of VAT) paid in instalments, plus travel, and an additional budget for materials for creative production, workshops and exhibition outputs (e.g. print). No application fee.

Duration: September 2026 to July 2027: workshops September-January, post-production to February 2027, UK and Czech tour March-July 2027

Deadline: 03 Aug 2026

Corridor seeks a socially-engaged artist based in the South East of England working with moving image / lens-based media for DAISY CHAIN, marking the 60th anniversary of Vera Chytilova's experimental film Daisies (1966). The commissioned artist will work with a group of LGBTQIA+ young people aged 15-26 in Adur (West Sussex) to co-create new artworks: a 2-3 minute moving image work and a series of 2D collage or mixed media artworks for public exhibition and screenings. DAISY CHAIN commissions six new artist moving image works overall (three England-based artists working with older women, young women and LGBTQIA+ youth; three artists in Czechia), developed in partnership with the National Film Museum in Prague (NaFilM) and Brighton-based videoclub, with results toured across England and Czechia in 2027. EXPECTATIONS: devise about eight hands-on workshops incorporating film, collage and mixed media (participants won't necessarily have an arts background); participate in 4-6 online peer sessions on collaborative practice led by artist Annis Joslin; complete exhibition-ready artworks on time and to budget; maintain a transparent dialogue on authorship with participants. Artists must have a participatory practice and experience of working creatively with young people. Note: to create a safe space, workshops will not be publicly labelled as LGBTQIA+. FEE: GBP 4,200 incl. VAT plus travel and a materials budget. TIMELINE: shortlist notified 7 August, online interviews 12 August 2026; launch event in Adur/Worthing March 2027. DEADLINE: 10am, 3 August 2026.

Open call details

item.title: Modern Art Oxford: Collaborative Micro-commissions Open Call 2026
item.description:
Organisation: Modern Art Oxford

Location: Oxford, UK. Open to collectives, duos, partnerships and collaborative groups based in the Arts Council England South East area (Oxfordshire, Berkshire, Buckinghamshire, Hampshire and Isle of Wight, Surrey, Kent, East Sussex, West Sussex).

Award: GBP 1,000 artist fee per selected collective, plus up to GBP 500 production budget, curatorial mentorship from the Modern Art Oxford team, four months of public exhibition display, professional installation photography, promotion, technical and production support, artwork transport support within the South East, peer networking, and inclusion in a public preview event. No application fee.

Duration: Production August to November 2026; install 23 November to 4 December 2026; exhibition 5 December 2026 to April 2027

Deadline: Closed 26 Jul 2026

Modern Art Oxford marks its 60th anniversary with an open call for three collaborative micro-commissions responding to the question: how can collective practice/s help us to embrace uncertainty and complexity? Collectives, duos, partnerships and collaborative groups based across the South East of England are invited to propose new small-scale experimental works for a group exhibition in the Ground Floor Gallery, running alongside a major solo exhibition by Mike Nelson, who is also on the selection panel. Proposals may take the form of multidisciplinary research, site-responsive work, grassroots organising, performance, visual art, sound, poetry or other creative practices; ideas should respond to the theme of collective practice and uncertainty, explore collaborative approaches, experiment across disciplines, be achievable within the budget and timeline, and be original to this open call (building on existing research is fine). WHO: groups of two or more people, including established artist collectives, newly formed collaborations, interdisciplinary partnerships, informal or community-led groups, and family collaborations, based in the Arts Council England South East area (Oxfordshire, Berkshire, Buckinghamshire, Hampshire and Isle of Wight, Surrey, Kent, East Sussex, West Sussex). SUPPORT: each of the three selected collectives receives a GBP 1,000 artist fee, up to GBP 500 production budget, curatorial mentorship, four months of exhibition display, installation photography, promotion, technical and production support, and transport support within the South East. TIMELINE: online briefing and Q&A 15 June 2026 (email creativelearning@modernartoxford.org.uk for the link); selection confirmed 14 August 2026; production August to November 2026; preview party 4 December 2026; exhibition 5 December 2026 to April 2027. Apply via Google Forms; an information pack PDF and FAQ are on the call page. DEADLINE: Sunday 26 July 2026, 23:59.

item.title: Serpentine Galleries: Live Programmes Curator
item.description:
Organisation: Serpentine Galleries

Location: London, United Kingdom; hybrid working (3 days in office, 2 remote).

Award: GBP 45,000 per year. Permanent role (3-month probation). No application fee.

Duration: Permanent appointment; hybrid, 3 days office / 2 remote. 25 days annual leave rising to 30 after 5 years, plus 8 bank holidays.

Deadline: Closed 10 Jul 2026

Serpentine Galleries seeks an experienced interdisciplinary Live Programmes Curator to initiate, develop, and produce a year-round live programme that extends and activates the gallery's exhibitions and curatorial vision through talks, performances, participatory experiences, and cross-disciplinary live formats. Building on Serpentine's flagship strands (the annual Marathons, Park Nights, Serpentine Cinema, and Study Days), the curator will run a live programme alongside and through onsite exhibitions, working closely with the Programmes, Production, and Audience teams. RESPONSIBILITIES: conceive, curate, and deliver live events (talks, performances, workshops, screenings, new formats); develop formats that bring visual artists into dialogue with dance, music, film, literature, technology, design, and social practice; lead planning and delivery on time and on budget; and develop programming that attracts new, diverse, and multi-generational audiences onsite and online. REQUIREMENTS: significant experience curating and/or producing live programmes in a gallery, museum, festival, performance, or cultural context; a strong interdisciplinary curatorial approach across multiple artistic forms; excellent project management, budgeting, and scheduling; strong communication and collaboration; and deep knowledge of contemporary art and current cultural discourse. TERMS: permanent role (3-month probationary period); hybrid working (3 days office, 2 remote); 25 days annual leave rising to 30 after 5 years plus 8 bank holidays; auto-enrolment pension, season-ticket loan, and Cycle2Work scheme. SALARY: GBP 45,000 per annum. TO APPLY: submit a CV and cover letter addressing how your skills fit the role, examples of relevant experience, and what attracts you to Serpentine. DEADLINE: midnight, 10 July 2026; first-stage interviews w/c 20 July 2026, second-stage w/c 27 July 2026.
